text:
maya.partnerships: Vendor updated their public roadmap — they plan a paired Gaudi microcode push and a small MI300 driver tweak in the same APAC week. Asking for coordinated maintenance + marketplace SKU refresh within 48h.

ren.apac-ops: Thanks. Can they split the pushes? Back-to-back maintenance increases rollback risk. Also need to know if MI300 requires node reboots.

maya.partnerships: They prefer separate pushes 48h apart: Gaudi first, MI300 later. MI300 needs driver warm-reload on most nodes; a small subset requires reboots. They've promised signed manifests and a compatibility matrix.

omar.platform: Marketplace impact: we can accept manifest POST and automate tagging, but we'll require schema fields: microcode_sha, driver_version, compatible_models. Will bump schema and pre-provision token.

zhao.eng-runtime: Runtime ops notes: For Gaudi canary keep batch size -10%, pre-warm KV cache, and pin Dedicated pools to avoid fallback spill. If MI300 driver causes kernel changes, we need an immediate tool to remap model-to-device affinity.

harpreet.si-lead: SI request: 90m dry run for each push with two SI engineers. Prefer at least 24h between dry run and push. Also need test accounts and a short test corpus for gen/embedding/rerank.

ren.apac-ops: Ops proposal:
- Gaudi canary: 2026-05-19 01:00-03:00 UTC (canary -> 4h monitor -> ramp)
- MI300 driver: 2026-05-21 02:00-04:00 UTC (canary -> 3h monitor -> ramp)
Dry runs 24h before each window, 90m slots.

omar.platform: I'll create schema v2.2, a staging ingest CI job, and a token for the vendor. We'll commit to a 48h SKU refresh SLA if manifests are signed and valid.

zhao.eng-runtime: Add runbook steps: fast-route switch script, KV cache warm, telemetry retention bump to 7d for the event window. Also, define fallback order: H100/H200 preferred, MI300 preferred for some model families, B200 last. If p95 > 2x baseline, trigger rollback.

harpreet.si-lead: SI will schedule slots. We need the compatibility matrix from vendor indicating which microcode triggers kernel fallbacks. Without it SI will treat any kernel changes as high-risk.

maya.partnerships: I'll push vendor ask: signed manifest 48h prior, compatibility matrix, list of nodes requiring reboot, and an outlined rollback procedure. Also ask if they want a joint announcement — they proposed 72h post-green.

ops-bot: Created maintenance entries: #gaudi-wedge-2026-05-19 (01:00-03:00Z), #mi300-driver-2026-05-21 (02:00-04:00Z). Incident stubs INC-6312 and INC-6313.

ren.apac-ops: Oncall rota: Ren (APAC morning), Keiko (APAC night), Zhao backup. I'll own incident coordination.

omar.platform: Action items: schema PR, token, CI job.

zhao.eng-runtime: I'll publish the runbook and route-switch scripts in #eng-runtime and prep the eval harness (3 workloads) for the dry runs.

harpreet.si-lead: SI action: confirm engineers and test corpus; will publish smoke test checklist.

maya.partnerships: I'll compile vendor ask doc and set a prep sync Fri EOD. If vendor confirms signed manifests, we'll lock the windows. :white_check_mark:
